entry.title: Collapse of a framed neat cobordism in $X\times I$
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $X$ be closed, $k\ge0$, and let $(W,\theta_0,\theta_1,\Psi)$ be a framed cobordism in $X\times I$ from $(N_0,\varphi_0)$ to $(N_1,\varphi_1)$. Choose a neat compatible tubular chart of $W$ in $X\times I$, a metric on $W\times\mathbb R^k$ and a radius, as in the DT-16 collapse definition. The collapse of the framed cobordism is the map $c_W:X\times I\to S^k$ that sends a point of the tube to its framed $\mathbb R^k$-coordinate in $S^k$ and every point outside the tube (including the added boundary basepoint copies) to the basepoint. It is continuous; its restrictions to $X\times\{0\}$ and $X\times\{1\}$ are the Pontryagin-Thom maps of $(N_0,\varphi_0)$ and $(N_1,\varphi_1)$ computed with the induced boundary tube data; hence $c_W$ is a homotopy between them.
entry.strategy: Instantiate DT-16's collapse definition with a boundary-adapted neat tube, using [[thm-neat-submanifolds-have-boundary-adapted-slice-charts]] and [[lem-tubular-charts-realize-a-prescribed-normal-identification]]; the collar product structure along the ends identifies the boundary restrictions with the boundaryless collapses of the $N_i$ in $X\cong X\times\{i\}$. Continuity follows from the closed-pasting argument of [[lem-collapse-map-is-continuous-and-smooth-away-from-the-basepoint]] applied to the compact tube and its complement in $X\times I$. The normal-data conventions and the restriction of the identification to the boundary are exactly the clauses of DT-16's [[lem-based-homotopies-transverse-to-the-zero-section-give-normal-cobordisms]]; countable choice is inherited from the compatible-chart existence.

entry.title: Framed cobordant submanifolds have homotopic Pontryagin-Thom maps
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $X$ be closed and let $(N_0,\varphi_0)$, $(N_1,\varphi_1)$ be closed framed codimension-$k$ submanifolds of $X$. If they are framed cobordant, then their Pontryagin-Thom maps $X\to S^k$ are homotopic, indeed based homotopic as maps $X_+\to S^k$, and a framed cobordism supplies an explicit homotopy $X\times I\to S^k$ whose end restrictions are the two maps up to based homotopy.
entry.strategy: Take the collapse $c_W$ of the framed cobordism from the previous item. Its end restrictions are Pontryagin-Thom maps of the boundary framed submanifolds computed with the induced tube data; [[lem-changing-framed-tube-data-changes-the-pontryagin-thom-map-by-based-homotopy]] identifies each of these with the Pontryagin-Thom map of the given framed data up to based homotopy. Concatenating the two based homotopies with $c_W$ gives the result. Compactness of $W$ and $X$ makes the tube compact and its complement closed, which is what the collapse uses.

entry.title: Framed regular preimages of a map to a sphere
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Fix the standard orientation of $S^k$ and identify $S^k=D^k/S^{k-1}$ with the one-point compactification $\mathbb R^k\cup\{\infty\}$ of the zero section of the trivial rank-$k$ bundle over a point, so the centre $y_0$ corresponds to $0$. Let $X$ be a closed smooth manifold, $f:X\to S^k$ smooth, $y\in S^k$ a regular value, and $b=(b_1,\dots,b_k)$ a positively oriented basis of $T_yS^k$, read as the trivialization $\beta:T_yS^k\to\mathbb R^k$. Then $N=f^{-1}(y)$ is a closed embedded submanifold of $X$ of codimension $k$, and the differential of $f$ factors through the normal quotient to a smooth bundle isomorphism $\nu(N\subseteq X)\to(f|_N)^*TS^k$; composing with $\beta$ gives a framing $f_*b:\nu(N\subseteq X)\to N\times\mathbb R^k$. The pair $(N,f_*b)$ is the framed regular preimage of $(f,y,b)$; well-definedness as a class is proved in the two following lemmas. Rank zero and $N=\varnothing$ are included.
entry.strategy: This is the special case $E=\mathbb R^k\times\{\mathrm{pt}\}$ of DT-16's [[prop-transverse-preimage-carries-a-pulled-back-normal-structure]]: the trivial rank-$k$ bundle over the one-point base has zero section $\{0\}\subseteq\mathbb R^k=D^k/S^{k-1}\subseteq S^k$, $f$ is smooth near the preimage, and transversality to the zero section is exactly regularity of $y$. Clauses (i)-(ii) of that proposition give the closed embedded submanifold and the identification of the normal bundle with the pullback; inserting the positive basis turns the target factor into $\mathbb R^k$, which is the framing. The countable-choice hypothesis is inherited exactly from that proposition.

entry.title: Positively oriented bases of an oriented vector space are path-connected
entry.statement: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space with an orientation. The set of positively oriented bases of $V$ is path-connected; equivalently $\mathrm{GL}^+(k,\mathbb R)$ is path-connected. In particular, for the oriented vector space $T_yS^k$, any two positive bases at $y$ can be joined by a continuous path of positive bases.
entry.strategy: Identify the positive bases with $\mathrm{GL}^+(k,\mathbb R)$ after fixing one basis. Factor an invertible matrix into elementary matrices ([[thm-invertible-matrices-factor-into-elementary-matrices]]): row-addition matrices lie on the path $I+tE$ and positive diagonal scalings on $(1-t)I+tD$, both inside $\mathrm{GL}^+$ for $t\in[0,1]$; the negative-determinant factors occur in an even number and can be paired so that each pair is a product of shears and positive scalings, each deformable to the identity. Equivalently, Gram-Schmidt reduces the problem to $\mathrm{SO}(k)$ and an oriented orthonormal frame is connected to the standard frame by finitely many plane rotations. Both are finite explicit constructions, so no choice principle is used.

entry.title: Homotopic maps with a common regular value have framed-cobordant preimages
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $X$ be closed and let $f_0,f_1:X\to S^k$ be smoothly homotopic maps for which $y\in S^k$ is a regular value of both, with a fixed positive basis $b$ of $T_yS^k$. Then the framed regular preimages $(f_0^{-1}(y),f_{0*}b)$ and $(f_1^{-1}(y),f_{1*}b)$ are framed cobordant. Consequently the framed class of a regular preimage is unchanged under smooth homotopy when the regular value is held fixed.
entry.strategy: Apply DT-16's [[lem-based-homotopies-transverse-to-the-zero-section-give-normal-cobordisms]] to the trivial rank-$k$ bundle over a point. Any continuous homotopy from $f_0$ to $f_1$ whose ends are smooth and transverse to the zero section near their zero preimages can be replaced by a based homotopy, fixed on the ends, that is smooth and transverse near its zero preimage; its zero preimage $W$ is a compact neat embedded submanifold of $X\times I$ whose normal bundle is identified with the pullback of the trivial bundle, i.e. carries a framing $\Psi$, and that identification restricts to the endpoint framings induced by $df_i$ and the same positive basis $b$. This is exactly a framed cobordism in the sense of the framed-cobordism definition; reparametrising the homotopy puts it in collar form.

entry.title: The framed preimage class is independent of regular value and positive basis
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $X$ be closed and $f:X\to S^k$ smooth. (i) At a regular value $y$, two positive bases $b,b'$ of $T_yS^k$ give framed-cobordant framed preimages $(N,f_*b)$ and $(N,f_*b')$. (ii) If $y,y'$ are regular values with positive bases $b,b'$, then the framed preimages are framed cobordant; consequently the framed cobordism class of a regular preimage depends only on the smooth homotopy class of $f$, and homotopic maps give framed-cobordant preimages for any choices of regular values and positive bases.
entry.strategy: (i) The change-of-basis matrix lies in $\mathrm{GL}^+(k,\mathbb R)$, which is path-connected by the previous lemma; a smooth path $b_t$ of positive bases through $b$ makes $(x,t)\mapsto f_*b_t$ a framing of the cylinder $N\times I\subseteq X\times I$ whose restrictions at the ends are $f_*b$ and $f_*b'$, so the cylinder is a framed cobordism. (ii) Choose an orientation-preserving rotation family $R_t$ of $S^k$ with $R_0=\mathrm{id}$ and $R_1(y)=y'$ (the explicit rotation in the plane spanned by $y,y'$, with the antipodal case handled by a perpendicular rotation), and put $F(x,t)=R_tf(x)$. Then $y'$ is a regular value of both $F_0=f$ and $F_1=R_1f$, because $(R_1f)^{-1}(y')=f^{-1}(y)$ and $d(R_1f)=dR_1\circ df$ is onto there; the homotopy lemma gives a framed cobordism between $(f^{-1}(y'),f_*b')$ and $(f^{-1}(y),f_*(b'\circ dR_1))$. Since $R_1$ is orientation-preserving, $b'\circ dR_1$ is a positive basis at $y$, so (i) identifies the second class with $(f^{-1}(y),f_*b)$. Combining the cobordisms yields (ii).

entry.title: The regular preimage of the collapse recovers the original framed submanifold
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $X$ be closed and $(N,\varphi)$ a closed framed codimension-$k$ submanifold, $k\ge1$, with Pontryagin-Thom map $f=f_{(N,\varphi)}:X\to S^k$. Then the centre $y_0$ (the image of the zero section under the structure identification) is a regular value of $f$, one has $f^{-1}(y_0)=N$, and the framing $f_*b$ determined by the positive basis $b$ of $T_{y_0}S^k$ corresponding to the structure identification is exactly $\varphi$. Thus the framed regular preimage of $(f,y_0,b)$ is $(N,\varphi)$ on the nose.
entry.strategy: In a compatible tube, $f$ is the composite of the tube coordinate $(s,v)\mapsto(s,v/\rho)$ with the framing and the quotient map to $D^k/S^{k-1}$. The vertical derivative at $(s,0)$ is the inverse of the framing (equivalently the framing, under the fixed identification convention), so $f$ is a submersion along $N$, its fibre over the centre is exactly $N$, and the induced normal framing is $\varphi$. This is the local computation of DT-16's [[lem-collapse-map-is-continuous-and-smooth-away-from-the-basepoint]] at the zero section, read through the framing identification of the Thom target. No choice is used beyond the tube data, which the tube-independence lemma removes.

entry.title: The collapse of a regular preimage is homotopic to the original map
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $X$ be closed, $f:X\to S^k$ smooth, $y$ a regular value with positive basis $b$, $(N,\varphi=f_*b)$ the framed preimage, and $g=f_{(N,\varphi)}$ its Pontryagin-Thom map. Then $g$ is smoothly homotopic to $f$ by a homotopy that is constant on a neighbourhood of $N$ and on the complement of a compact tube; in particular the collapse-after-preimage composition is the identity on smooth homotopy classes.
entry.strategy: Choose a tubular chart of $N$ in $X$ on which $f$ takes the normal form given by its differential, using [[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]] and the regular-value hypothesis. First homotope $f$, localized in the tube and equal to the collapse map outside, so that $f$ and $g$ agree on a smaller tube and have the same derivative along $N$: this is the cutoff deformation along the framing coordinate (Freed (3.13)/Milnor Lemma 4). Then deform inside the affine chart $S^k\setminus\{\text{antipode}\}$ by the straight-line homotopy between the two maps, which is well defined because the maps agree near $N$ and agree with the collapse (hence avoid the antipode) outside a neighbourhood of $N$; this is Milnor's Lemma 4. Every homotopy is fixed on the complement of a compact tube, hence on any prescribed closed set missed by the tube, and the pasting uses [[lem-continuity-is-local-and-pastes]].

entry.title: Based and free homotopy classes of maps between spheres agree
entry.statement: For $n,k\ge1$ the forgetful map $\pi_n(S^k)\to[S^n,S^k]$ from based homotopy classes to free homotopy classes of continuous maps is a bijection (a based homotopy is in particular a free homotopy, so the map is well defined).
entry.strategy: Surjectivity: given $f:S^n\to S^k$, choose an explicit path of rotations $R_t$ of $S^k$ with $R_1(f(*))=*$ (rotate in the two-plane spanned by $f(*)$ and $*$; if they are antipodal use a perpendicular intermediate rotation); then $R_t\circ f$ is a free homotopy from $f$ to the based map $R_1\circ f$. Injectivity: a free homotopy between based maps $f_0,f_1$ is a map $F:D^{n+1}\to S^k$ on the disk with boundary values $f_0$ and $f_1$; precomposing $F$ with a self-homotopy-equivalence of the disk that carries the radial segment from the centre to the boundary basepoint into the basepoint and fixes that boundary basepoint produces a based homotopy from $f_0$ to $f_1$ (Freed's Figure 13 argument). Both steps are explicit and use no choice principle.

entry.title: The Pontryagin-Thom correspondence in fixed codimension
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge k\ge1$ the collapse construction and the framed-regular-preimage construction define mutually inverse bijections between the set of framed cobordism classes of closed framed $(n-k)$-submanifolds of $S^n$ and the $n$-th homotopy group $\pi_n(S^k)$; equivalently, they give a bijection with the set $[S^n,S^k]$ of free homotopy classes of continuous maps. This is the Pontryagin-Thom theorem in fixed codimension, with the empty preimage and the rank-zero conventions included.
entry.strategy: Define $\Phi$ from framed cobordism classes to $\pi_n(S^k)$ by the Pontryagin-Thom map: the previous cobordism-to-homotopy lemma makes it well defined. Define $\Psi$ from $\pi_n(S^k)$ to framed cobordism classes by replacing a class with a smooth representative ([[cor-every-continuous-map-between-smooth-manifolds-is-homotopic-to-a-smooth-map]], [[thm-continuously-homotopic-smooth-maps-are-smoothly-homotopic]]), choosing a regular value and a positive basis ([[thm-morse-sard-for-smooth-manifolds]], [[cor-regular-values-form-a-dense-g-delta-set]]) and taking the framed regular preimage; the two independence lemmas make $\Psi$ well defined. The recovery lemma shows $\Psi\circ\Phi=\mathrm{id}$ at the level of framed classes, and the collapse-after-preimage lemma shows $\Phi\circ\Psi=\mathrm{id}$ on homotopy classes. Finally the based/free lemma identifies $\pi_n(S^k)$ with free homotopy classes. The hypotheses $n\ge k\ge1$ keep the preimage dimension nonnegative and the target sphere positive-dimensional.

entry.title: Stabilized framed cobordism and the framed bordism group
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $d\ge0$ and $k\ge1$ let $\mathrm{Cob}_d(k)$ be the set of framed cobordism classes of closed framed $d$-submanifolds of $S^{d+k}$ (codimension $k$; the fixed-codimension theorem applies with $n=d+k\ge k$). The equatorial stabilization $\sigma:\mathrm{Cob}_d(k)\to\mathrm{Cob}_d(k+1)$ sends the class of $(N,\varphi)$ to the class of $(i(N),\varphi\oplus\nu_{\mathrm{eq}})$, where $i:S^{d+k}\hookrightarrow S^{d+k+1}$ is the equatorial inclusion and $\nu_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the outward unit normal framing of the equator; framed cobordisms are carried to framed cobordisms by $i\times\mathrm{id}_I$, so $\sigma$ is well defined. The framed bordism group $\Omega^{\mathrm{fr}}_d$ is the colimit of $\mathrm{Cob}_d(1)\to\mathrm{Cob}_d(2)\to\cdots$, i.e. the quotient of $\bigsqcup_{k\ge1}\mathrm{Cob}_d(k)$ that identifies $s$ with $\sigma(s)$; disjoint union of representatives in disjoint affine charts makes it an abelian group with the empty manifold as zero, compatibly with stabilization. This is the group of framed cobordisms of closed $d$-manifolds (Ranicki's Definition 6.16, Freed's Proposition 5.21): a stable framing is a stabilization class of actual normal framings in spheres, and no representative lives in a fixed sphere.
entry.strategy: Well-definedness of $\sigma$: the equatorial inclusion is a smooth embedding, its image is a framed submanifold with framing $\varphi\oplus\nu_{\mathrm{eq}}$, and a framed cobordism in $S^{d+k}\times I$ maps to a framed cobordism in $S^{d+k+1}\times I$ under $i\times\mathrm{id}$ with the framings related by the constant normal field; hence classes map to classes. Group structure: represent two classes at a common large level in two disjoint affine charts as in DT-15's [[thm-disjoint-union-makes-bordism-classes-abelian-groups]]; the operation is compatible with the stabilizations, so it descends to the colimit, and the inverse of a class is represented by the same manifold with the framing reflected in one normal direction, since the cylinder with the interpolated framing bounds the disjoint union. Countable choice is inherited from the framed-cobordism relation.

entry.title: Stabilizing a framed submanifold suspends its Pontryagin-Thom map
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $d\ge0$, $k\ge1$ and let $(N,\varphi)$ be a closed framed $d$-submanifold of $S^{d+k}$ with Pontryagin-Thom map $f:S^{d+k}\to S^k$. Let $\sigma(N,\varphi)\subseteq S^{d+k+1}$ be its equatorial stabilization and $E:\pi_{d+k}(S^k)\to\pi_{d+k+1}(S^{k+1})$ the suspension homomorphism determined by the sphere-prespectrum homeomorphism $S^1\wedge S^k\cong S^{k+1}$. Then the Pontryagin-Thom class of $\sigma(N,\varphi)$ is the suspension of the class of $(N,\varphi)$: $\mathrm{PT}(\sigma(N,\varphi))=E(\mathrm{PT}(N,\varphi))$ in $\pi_{d+k+1}(S^{k+1})$. The same identity holds for the stabilized classes under $\sigma$.
entry.strategy: Identify $S^{d+k+1}$ with the reduced suspension of $S^{d+k}$ in the two-cone model with the equator as the middle slice ([[def-reduced-cone-suspension-and-cofiber-sequence]]). The tube of $\sigma(N)$ is the product of a tube of $N$ with the added normal direction, so its collapse map is the suspension of the collapse map of $N$; this uses DT-16's [[lem-stabilizing-a-normal-bundle-suspends-its-thom-space]] to identify $\operatorname{Th}(\nu\oplus\varepsilon^1)\cong\operatorname{Th}(\nu)\wedge S^1$ and the naturality of the framing identification, which turns the suspension of the composed map into the suspension followed by the homeomorphism $S^k\wedge S^1\cong S^{k+1}$ used to define $E$. Framed cobordisms stabilize by the same construction, so the identity descends to $\mathrm{Cob}_d(k)\to\mathrm{Cob}_d(k+1)$.

entry.title: The stable Pontryagin-Thom theorem identifies framed bordism with stable stems
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every $d\ge0$ the levelwise Pontryagin-Thom bijections $\mathrm{Cob}_d(k)\to\pi_{d+k}(S^k)$ are compatible with the stabilization maps $\sigma$ and the suspension homomorphisms $E$, and hence induce a bijection $\Omega^{\mathrm{fr}}_d\to\pi_d^s$ between the framed bordism group of closed $d$-manifolds and the $d$-th stable stem of the sphere. The bijection is an isomorphism of abelian groups for disjoint union on the left and addition in $\pi_d^s$ on the right; it is the stable Pontryagin-Thom theorem.
entry.strategy: The stabilization lemma gives a morphism of directed systems from $(\mathrm{Cob}_d(k),\sigma)$ to $(\pi_{d+k}(S^k),E)$ that is levelwise bijective by the fixed-codimension theorem, so passing to the colimit gives a bijection of the colimits: a class in the colimit is represented at some finite level, and two representatives agree after further stabilization. The right-hand colimit is $\pi_d^s$ by definition ([[def-stable-stem-of-the-sphere]]), with [[prop-the-sphere-prespectrum-homotopy-groups-are-the-stable-stems]] and [[lem-freudenthal-identifies-the-eventual-suspension-system-for-spheres]] identifying its eventual value. Additivity: two classes can be represented at a common large level in disjoint affine charts, and the collapse of a disjoint union is the pinch composite of the two collapse maps, which is the sum in $\pi_{d+k}(S^k)$ (Milnor's union remark; the group law on the colimit is disjoint union by the definition item). Both sides are compatible with stabilization, so the isomorphism is additive.

entry.title: Normal framings, stable normal framings and tangential framings are distinct data
entry.statement: An actual normal framing, a stable normal framing (a trivialization of the stable normal bundle after the relevant trivial summands are added), and a stable tangential framing (a trivialization of $TM\oplus\varepsilon^j$) are three different data types. A normal framing of $N\subseteq S^m$ determines a stable tangential framing, and after a splitting of the ambient tangent sequence and the stable trivialization of $TS^m$ it corresponds to a stable normal framing up to homotopy; an actual framing of $\nu(N)$ is not a trivialization of the stable class, and a stable framing neither singles out a level $k$ nor an embedding. In particular the elements of $\Omega^{\mathrm{fr}}_d$ are stabilization classes, not framed submanifolds of a fixed sphere; only at a sufficiently large level does a representative become an actual framed submanifold.
entry.strategy: Convention remark; the identification of stable normal and stable tangential framings is Freed Proposition 5.19, and the passage from an actual framing of an equatorially embedded submanifold to a stable framing is the stabilization of the definition item. The warning is exactly that the three structures are not silently interchangeable and that the stable theorem's left-hand side is a colimit.

entry.title: Framed zero-manifolds and signed points
entry.statement: For $n\ge1$, a closed framed $0$-dimensional submanifold of $S^n$ is a finite set of points, each framed by a basis of $T_xS^n$; call the framing positive when that basis is positively oriented for the standard orientation of $S^n$, and let $\mathrm{sgn}(x)=\pm1$ accordingly. Framed cobordism classes of such points are classified by the signed count $\sum_x\mathrm{sgn}(x)\in\mathbb Z$: under the fixed-codimension correspondence with $k=n$ the signed count is the degree of the Pontryagin-Thom map $S^n\to S^n$, and $\pi_n(S^n)\cong\mathbb Z$ by degree. A single positively framed point realizes $+1$, its orientation reversal $-1$, and the empty $0$-manifold $0$.
entry.strategy: Local computation: on a coordinate ball around a point, the collapse of a positively framed point is a degree-$+1$ map of the ball onto $S^n$ (the boundary of the ball goes to the basepoint); a negatively framed point gives degree $-1$. Disjoint union of framed points gives the pinched sum of the collapse maps, which is addition of degrees. Comparing with the fixed-codimension bijection and the degree isomorphism $\pi_n(S^n)\cong\mathbb Z$ gives the classification.

entry.title: The Pontryagin-Thom map of the standard framed equator
entry.statement:
For $m\ge1$ let $S^{m-1}\subseteq S^m$ be the equator, framed by the outward
unit normal of the closed northern hemisphere. The standard hemisphere sweep
in $S^m\times I$ is a compact neat framed cobordism from this framed equator to
the empty manifold, so the framed equator is framed null-cobordant and its
Pontryagin-Thom map $S^m\to S^1$ is nullhomotopic; for $m=1$ the two equator
points carry opposite signs and the signed count is $0$. The equator is the
equatorial stabilization of the equator one dimension lower, so the example
exhibits the $\sigma$-to-$E$ compatibility on the trivial class, in contrast
with the generator of the corresponding stable stem, which is represented by a
single positively framed point.
entry.strategy: A null-cobordism of the framed equator is obtained by the standard hemisphere sweep in $S^m\times I$: the graph of a boundary-defining function over the closed northern hemisphere, carrying the induced normal framing, is a compact neat framed cobordism from the framed equator to the empty manifold, with endpoint collars straightened as in the framed-cobordism definition. Then the cobordism-to-homotopy lemma makes the Pontryagin-Thom map nullhomotopic. The stabilization statement is the compatibility lemma applied to the canonical equators, and the generator contrast is the framed-point example together with degree classification.

entry.title: The framed unknot represents a generator of $\pi_3(S^2)$
entry.statement: Let $h:S^3\subseteq\mathbb C^2\to\mathbb CP^1\cong S^2$, $h(z_1,z_2)=[z_1:z_2]$, be the Hopf map. The fibre over $[1:0]$ is the standard unknot $U=\{z_2=0\}\cong S^1$, and the differential of $h$ at the regular value $[1:0]$ frames the normal bundle of $U$ in $S^3$; let $(U,h_*b)$ be this framed unknot. Then the Pontryagin-Thom map of $(U,h_*b)$ is homotopic to $h$, and since the Hopf fibration's long exact sequence gives $h_*:\pi_3(S^3)\to\pi_3(S^2)$ an isomorphism while $\pi_3(S^3)\cong\mathbb Z$, the class of the framed unknot is a generator of $\pi_3(S^2)\cong\mathbb Z$. No Hopf-invariant theory is developed.
entry.strategy: The fibre $U$ is a closed embedded circle and $[1:0]$ is a regular value of the smooth map $h$; the framed regular preimage is $(U,h_*b)$ by definition. The collapse-after-preimage lemma gives a smooth homotopy from its Pontryagin-Thom map to $h$. For the homotopy groups: the Hopf map is a numerable circle bundle hence a Hurewicz fibration; its long exact sequence contains $\pi_3(S^1)\to\pi_3(S^3)\to\pi_3(S^2)\to\pi_2(S^1)$, where $\pi_k(S^1)=0$ for $k\ge2$ by the contractible universal cover and $\pi_2(S^3)=\pi_1(S^3)=0$ by the lower-dimensional nullhomotopy theorem; exactness makes $h_*$ an isomorphism, and $\pi_3(S^3)\cong\mathbb Z$ by degree classification. Hence $\pi_3(S^2)\cong\mathbb Z$ with generator the class of $h$, and the framed unknot's class is that generator.

entry.title: A framing, not just the submanifold, determines the Pontryagin-Thom class
entry.statement:
The Pontryagin-Thom class of a framed submanifold depends only on the
underlying submanifold, not on the framing.
entry.strategy: The unknot $U=\{z_2=0\}\subseteq S^3$ bounds the disk $\{z\in S^3:\mathrm{Im}(z_2)=0,\ \mathrm{Re}(z_2)\ge0\}\cong D^2$; framing that disk by its normal line restricts to a framing of $U$ under which $U$ is framed null-cobordant, and then the cobordism-to-homotopy lemma makes the Pontryagin-Thom map nullhomotopic. The Hopf framing gives a generator by the previous example. A generator of $\mathbb Z$ is not $0$, so the two maps are not homotopic.

entry.title: Stabilizing a framed point suspends its collapse map
entry.statement:
Let $p\in S^1$ be a single positively framed point; its Pontryagin-Thom map
is the degree-$+1$ self-map of $S^1$, the generator of
$\pi_1(S^1)\cong\mathbb Z$ (the framed-point example). Its equatorial
stabilization is the same point in $S^2$ with the prepended normal framing,
whose Pontryagin-Thom map is the suspension $E$ of the degree-$+1$ map, i.e.
the degree-$+1$ self-map of $S^2$, the generator of
$\pi_2(S^2)\cong\mathbb Z$. Iterating, the stabilization of the positively
framed point of $S^k$ is the positively framed point of $S^{k+1}$ and the
classes are related by the suspension isomorphisms
$E:\pi_k(S^k)\to\pi_{k+1}(S^{k+1})$. This verifies the
stabilization-to-suspension compatibility on a nonzero class.
entry.strategy: Apply the general stabilization lemma to the positively framed point in $S^1$; the suspension of the degree-one self-map of $S^1$ is the degree-one self-map of $S^2$ under the sphere-prespectrum homeomorphism, and both are generators by the degree classification. Iteration uses the same lemma level by level.

entry.title: The frame bundle of a smooth manifold
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), inherited from the smooth tangent-bundle theorem. Let $M$ be a smooth $m$-manifold with $m\ge1$. Its tangent bundle
$TM=\bigsqcup_{x\in M}T_xM$ carries the canonical smooth $2m$-manifold
structure of [[thm-the-tangent-bundle-has-a-canonical-smooth-2n-manifold-structure]]
([[def-tangent-bundle-as-a-disjoint-union]], [[def-smooth-manifold]]). The
**frame bundle** of $M$ is the frame bundle of the tangent bundle in the sense
of [[def-frame-bundle-and-associated-vector-bundle]],
$$B(M):=\operatorname{Fr}(TM)=\{(x,b):x\in M,\ b:\mathbb R^m\to T_xM\ \text{a linear isomorphism}\},$$
the total space of the principal $\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbb R)$-bundle of
[[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]] associated with $TM$. It
carries the smooth structure induced by the linear bundle charts of $TM$
(locally $U\times\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbb R)$, the second factor an open subset of
the matrix space), the smooth projection $\pi:B(M)\to M$, $\pi(x,b)=x$, and the
free smooth right action $(x,b)\cdot A=(x,b\circ A)$ of
$\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbb R)$, whose orbits are exactly the fibres $B(M)_x$; each
fibre is therefore a $\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbb R)$-torsor. A **framing of the
point $x\in M$** is an element $(x,b)$ of the fibre $B(M)_x$, equivalently a
linear isomorphism $b:\mathbb R^m\to T_xM$.

The fibre $B(M)_x$ has exactly two path components, the two orientation
classes of bases of $T_xM$ ([[def-orientation-of-a-finite-dimensional-real-vector-space]]).
Indeed the determinant $\det:\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbb R)\to\mathbb R^\times$ is a
surjective continuous group homomorphism
([[cor-operator-determinant-on-the-general-linear-group]]), so its sign
separates $\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbb R)$ into the nonempty open sets of positive
and negative determinant, and the torsor action identifies these with $B(M)_x$;
left multiplication by $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,\ldots,1)$ identifies the negative-determinant matrices with the positive-determinant matrices, which are path-connected by
[[lem-positively-oriented-bases-are-path-connected]], so these are exactly the two path components. When $M$ is oriented, a chart of $M$ whose coordinate frame
is positive at a point gives the identification of $B(M)_x$ with the positive
and negative bases used here ([[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]).

A **framing of a closed $0$-dimensional submanifold $N\subseteq M$** is a
framing of $N$ in $M$ in the sense of the normal-quotient convention: since
$\dim N=0$, the normal bundle $\nu(N\subseteq M)=\coprod_{x\in N}T_xM/T_xN$
is $\coprod_{x\in N}T_xM$ over the discrete set $N$
([[def-normal-and-conormal-bundles-of-an-embedded-submanifold]]), so a framing
of $N$ is exactly a family $(b_x)_{x\in N}$ of linear isomorphisms
$b_x:\mathbb R^m\to T_xM$, that is, a family of framings of the individual
points $x\in N$. If $N$ is compact it is finite: its singleton subsets form an open cover and admit a finite subcover.

Finally, if $M$ is oriented, the **sign** of a framing $(x,b)$ is
$\varepsilon(b)=+1$ when the isomorphism $b$ carries the standard orientation
of $\mathbb R^m$ (the one for which the standard basis is positive) to the
given orientation of $T_xM$, and $\varepsilon(b)=-1$ otherwise. Two framings
of the same point have the same sign exactly when they lie in the same
component of $B(M)_x$: the sign is constant on a component because it is a
continuous function with values in $\{\pm1\}$, and the two components are the
positive and the negative bases for the given orientation. No orientation of
$M$ is needed for the definition of $B(M)$ or of a framing, and this definition
selects nothing beyond the supplied chart data of $M$.
entry.strategy: Compared Fr(TM) with its published bundle definition and the AC_omega tangent smooth-structure theorem. Right action b composed with A has correct type. Positive matrices are connected; multiplication by a fixed reflection proves negative connectivity, giving exactly two fibre components for m>=1. The normal quotient of a discrete 0-submanifold is T_xM; compactness alone supplies finiteness, preserving infinite discrete sets in noncompact M. Reader corrections are sound.

entry.title: The components of the frame bundle of a connected manifold
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a nonempty connected smooth $m$-manifold, $m\ge1$. If $M$ is orientable, $B(M)$ has exactly two components, corresponding to the positive and negative frames for either fixed orientation of $M$. If $M$ is nonorientable, $B(M)$ is connected. Each component is locally path-connected, and any two of its frames are joined by a smooth path. In the oriented case the endpoint frames of such a path have the same sign.
entry.strategy: Checked the authored tangent-ray cover rather than the obsolete orientation-cover scaffold. Transition determinant signs are locally constant; path lifting over a connected nonempty base gives at most two sheets/components, and two components each project bijectively and yield an orientation section. A section and its opposite give two components. Finite bundle-trivialization lifts connect frame paths, with endpoint adjustment in GL^+. Plateau reparametrization and extension to R satisfy the relative Whitney theorem's smooth-near-closed-set hypothesis. m>=1 and nonemptiness are essential; AC_omega carried.

entry.title: Framed points joined by a path of framings are framed cobordant
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed smooth $m$-manifold, $m\ge1$,
and let $c:[0,1]\to B(M)$ be a smooth path in the frame bundle from
$(x_0,b_0)$ to $(x_1,b_1)$. Then the framed points $(x_0,b_0)$ and
$(x_1,b_1)$, regarded as closed framed $0$-dimensional submanifolds of $M$ of
codimension $m$ with framings $b_i:\mathbb R^m\to T_{x_i}M$, are framed
cobordant in $M$.
entry.strategy: Checked lambda=sigma(3t-1) has endpoint plateaux containing width 1/8. Graph embedding is injective with nonzero time derivative and compact image; it is neat with literal product ends. Q_t(v,a)=v-a gamma_dot has precisely the graph tangent kernel, so b(lambda(t)) inverse composed with Q_t is a smooth normal-quotient framing. On collars Q_t(v,a)=v and the framing equals endpoint data. The argument does not require disjoint-union machinery.

entry.title: Disjoint unions of framed cobordisms
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold and $k\ge0$.
Let $(W_N,\varepsilon_N,\Psi_N)$ and $(W_L,\varepsilon_L,\Psi_L)$ be framed
codimension-$k$ cobordisms in $M\times I$, from $(N_0,\varphi_0)$ to
$(N_1,\varphi_1)$ and from $(L_0,\psi_0)$ to $(L_1,\psi_1)$, respectively.
If their images are disjoint, then their union, with the combined framing
and collar width $\min(\varepsilon_N,\varepsilon_L)$, is a framed cobordism
from $(N_0\sqcup L_0,\varphi_0\sqcup\psi_0)$ to
$(N_1\sqcup L_1,\varphi_1\sqcup\psi_1)$.

Disjoint endpoint sets alone do not assert disjointness of the cobordisms.
This lemma does not assert that arbitrary embedded framed cobordism classes
in a fixed $M$ form a monoid. For finite disjoint sets of framed points,
cardinality modulo two is additive, and, when $M$ is oriented, the sum of
framing signs is additive.
entry.strategy: Given cobordisms with disjoint compact images, their closedness separates the pieces locally. Step 1.1 proves compact neat embedded union; step 2.1 pastes normal framings and takes the admissible minimum collar width. Finite counts add. No arbitrary-codimension monoid is asserted.

entry.title: The framing sign of a zero-dimensional regular preimage
entry.statement:
Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, inherited from the framed
preimage of [[def-framed-regular-preimage-of-a-map-to-a-sphere]]. Let $M$ be a
closed oriented smooth $m$-manifold with $m\ge1$, and let $(N,\varphi)$ be a
closed framed $0$-dimensional submanifold of $M$ in the sense of
[[def-framing-of-a-normal-bundle]]. Since $\dim N=0$, the normal bundle of $N$
in $M$ is $\nu(N\subseteq M)=\coprod_{x\in N}T_xM/T_xN=\coprod_{x\in N}T_xM$
over the finite set $N$
([[def-normal-and-conormal-bundles-of-an-embedded-submanifold]]), and the
framing is a family of linear isomorphisms
$\varphi_x:T_xM\to\mathbb R^m$; the pair $(x,\varphi_x)$ is a framing of the
point $x$ in the frame-bundle dictionary of
[[def-frame-bundle-of-a-smooth-manifold]], namely the inverse of the element
$(x,\varphi_x^{-1})\in B(M)_x$.

The **framing sign** of $x\in N$ is
$$\varepsilon(x):=\begin{cases}+1,&\varphi_x\ \text{is orientation-preserving for the given orientation of}\ T_xM\ \text{and the standard orientation of}\ \mathbb R^m,\\ -1,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}$$
and the **signed count** of $(N,\varphi)$ is
$\Phi(N,\varphi):=\sum_{x\in N}\varepsilon(x)\in\mathbb Z$. Replacing
$\varphi_x$ by $A\circ\varphi_x$ for $A\in\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbb R)$ multiplies
$\varepsilon(x)$ by the sign of $\det A$, so the sign records exactly the
orientation class of the framing and is constant on the two components of the
fibre $B(M)_x$; when $M$ is oriented and a positive chart is used,
$\varepsilon(x)=+1$ precisely for the positively oriented framings of
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]] and
[[def-orientation-of-a-finite-dimensional-real-vector-space]]. The empty
$0$-manifold has signed count $0$, and the definition uses no choice beyond the
inherited $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and no orientation when only the unframed parity
of $N$ is considered.

For the **framed regular preimage** of a smooth map $f:M\to S^m$ at a regular
value $y$ with a positive basis $b$ of $T_yS^m$, write $\beta:T_yS^m\to\mathbb R^m$ for the coordinate isomorphism sending the positive basis $b$ to the standard basis. The induced framing is
$f_*b=\beta\circ df_x$ on $\nu(x)=T_xM$
([[def-framed-regular-preimage-of-a-map-to-a-sphere]]), and the framing sign of
$x\in f^{-1}(y)$ is exactly the **local orientation sign**
$\operatorname{sgn}(df_x)$ of
[[def-local-orientation-sign-of-a-regular-preimage]]: both compare the
isomorphism $df_x:T_xM\to T_yS^m$ of oriented vector spaces, and the positive
coordinate isomorphism $\beta$ carries the given orientation of $T_yS^m$ to the standard orientation
of $\mathbb R^m$. In particular the signed count of the framed preimage is the
sum of the local orientation signs of $f$ over the regular fibre.
entry.strategy: Framing direction is T_xM to R^m, inverse to the frame-bundle element. Postcomposition A composed with phi_x is correctly typed and multiplies sign by det A. Positive target coordinate beta composed with df_x has the local degree sign; finite N follows from closedness in compact M. Empty signed sum is zero. entry.title: Oppositely framed points are framed null-cobordant in pairs
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed smooth $m$-manifold, $m\ge1$,
let $U\subseteq M$ be the domain of a chart with image an open ball in
$\mathbb R^m$, and let $x_0,x_1\in U$ be distinct points with framings
$\varphi_0,\varphi_1$ such that, in the chart coordinates, the bases
$\varphi_0,\varphi_1$ induce opposite orientations of $\mathbb R^m$. Then the
closed framed $0$-dimensional submanifold
$\{(x_0,\varphi_0)\}\sqcup\{(x_1,\varphi_1)\}$ of $M$ is framed null-cobordant
by a framed cobordism $W\subseteq U\times I$ supported in $U$; equivalently, in
the orientable chart ball the two points have opposite framing signs. The cobordism can be taken to be a smooth staple with vertical product ends at the actual two points, preceded by changes of framing on their disjoint stationary cylinders.
entry.strategy: Verified the staple at the actual points: a=d sigma(3s-1) is increasing in the middle; t=hs(1-s) is positive inside and monotone on distinct endpoint legs. Its derivative never vanishes, and compactness gives an embedded arc with literal bottom collars. The normal pair w1=(-t'e1,a')/q and tangent (a'e1,t') has determinant q>0; endpoint normal signs are opposite. Reversing w1 swaps them. Prescribed frames connect to model frames on disjoint stationary cylinders and glue by the exact equivalence supplier. The chart ball contains the entire segment. Works for m=1, distinct points, either sign ordering, and no unsupported union or model-point relocation.

entry.title: The signed count is invariant under framed cobordism
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed oriented smooth $m$-manifold,
$m\ge1$, and let $(N_0,\varphi_0)$, $(N_1,\varphi_1)$ be closed framed
$0$-dimensional submanifolds of $M$ with signed counts $\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1$. If
they are framed cobordant then $\Sigma_0=\Sigma_1$. In particular a closed
framed $0$-manifold containing exactly two points of the same framing sign and
no other points is not framed null-cobordant, while a pair of points of
opposite framing signs lying in a common chart ball is framed null-cobordant.
entry.strategy: Checked product orientation with M before time: ambient bottom/top face signs are (-1)^(m+1), (-1)^m. More directly, normal-before-tangent orients W by epsilon(x) partial_t on a collar. Its induced endpoint signs are -epsilon at bottom and +epsilon at top. Exact compact-boundary fundamental class and H_0 augmentation imply zero total boundary count, hence Sigma0=Sigma1, including empty configurations and disconnected M/W. Same-sign pair has count +/-2 and cannot cancel; opposite chart pair uses the earlier staple. Reader sign correction retained.

entry.title: Framed 0-manifolds in an oriented manifold are classified by the integers
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a nonempty closed connected oriented smooth
$m$-manifold, $m\ge1$. Then the signed count
$\Phi(N,\varphi)=\sum_{x\in N}\varepsilon(x)$ is a bijection from the set of
framed cobordism classes of closed framed $0$-dimensional submanifolds of $M$
to $\mathbb Z$, it is additive under disjoint union, and $(N,\varphi)$ is
framed null-cobordant if and only if $\Phi(N,\varphi)=0$. Framed cobordism
classes of closed framed $0$-manifolds in $M$ therefore form a commutative
monoid isomorphic to $(\mathbb Z,+)$.
entry.strategy: Signed count is invariant and each integer has finite same-sign representatives. For m>=2, checked punctured-ball avoidance and chartwise frame transport that leaves stationary cylinders disjoint; cancellation is confined to separate chart supports. For m=1, the actual compact-one-manifold classification identifies an oriented circle. Adjacent opposite cyclic signs cancel; two remaining same-sign configurations have cyclically ordered lifts whose convex interpolation retains all positive cyclic gaps, including the closing gap. Endpoint frames adjust on disjoint cylinders, and flattened graph framings give an embedded cobordism. Equal counts imply cobordism, converse follows from invariant, zero includes empty configuration. Addition is justified only after the count bijection and disjoint representatives, so it does not use the defective arbitrary-codimension monoid claim. All inherited choice explicit.

entry.title: Framed 0-manifolds in a nonorientable manifold are classified by parity
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed connected nonorientable smooth
$m$-manifold, $m\ge1$. Then the parity $N\mapsto|N|\bmod2$ is a bijection from
the set of framed cobordism classes of closed framed $0$-dimensional
submanifolds of $M$ to $\mathbb Z/2$, it is additive under disjoint union, and
$(N,\varphi)$ is framed null-cobordant if and only if $|N|$ is even. No
orientation of $M$ is used to define the invariant.
entry.strategy: Read the actual published compact-one-manifold classification/parity statement and proof: cobordism boundaries have even cardinality. A closed connected one-manifold is a circle and orientable, so nonorientable M has m>=2 and is nonempty. Checked punctured-ball paths via an intermediate point outside finitely many lines; chartwise frame transport preserves local determinant components and avoids all stationary cylinders. Connected B(M) permits opposite terminal chart framings; successive disjoint-support cancellations reduce to empty or singleton. Singleton cannot cancel by parity; any singleton frames are cobordant. Disjoint representatives then define addition using the proved parity bijection. Both directions of null iff even and both parities verified, without the false general union lemma.

entry.title: The Pontryagin-Thom signed preimage count equals the degree
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a nonempty closed connected oriented smooth

and $b$ a positive basis of $T_yS^m$. Then the framed regular preimage
$(f^{-1}(y),f_*b)$ has signed count
$\sum_{x\in f^{-1}(y)}\varepsilon(x)=\deg(f)$, the compact-support degree of
$f$; equivalently $\varepsilon(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(df_x)$ at every
$x\in f^{-1}(y)$. No new definition of degree is introduced.
entry.strategy: The induced framing is explicitly beta composed with df on T_xM/0; positive beta makes its sign exactly the local orientation sign. The exact regular-value degree theorem applies to the nonempty connected oriented closed source and connected sphere for m>=1. Compactness makes the map proper and the fibre finite. Summation includes an empty regular fibre, giving degree zero. Reader basis/trivialization and nonempty-domain corrections retained.

entry.title: Every integer is realized by a map to the sphere
entry.statement:
Let $M$ be a nonempty closed connected oriented smooth $m$-manifold with $m\ge1$. For
every $k\in\mathbb Z$ there is a smooth map $f:M\to S^m$ with
$\deg(f)=k$. The construction is explicit. Choose $|k|$ pairwise disjoint
closed coordinate balls in $M$, with charts $\varphi_i$; on the $i$-th ball the
map is the smooth model pinch $F$ of step 2.1 below, read in the chart, and it
is the base point $N$ of $S^m$ outside the balls. The model has a regular
value $y_-$ whose only preimage is the centre of the ball, and it is constant
with value $N$ outside the unit ball, so the centres are the only preimages of
$y_-$ under $f$ and $y_-$ is a regular value there. Hence
$\deg(f)=\sum_{i=1}^{|k|}\operatorname{sgn}(df_{p_i})$, and choosing each chart
orientation-preserving or orientation-reversing makes every summand equal to
$\operatorname{sgn}(k)$, so that $\deg(f)=k$; for $k=0$ the empty family gives
the constant map of degree $0$. The construction uses only finite choice and no
other form of the Axiom of Choice.
entry.strategy: Checked W=s near zero, W=1 beyond 3/4, positivity for s>0 and smooth cutoff Phi. The sphere norm identity holds; y_- has only preimage zero with derivative 2I. Disjoint open chart domains and compact closed subballs justify smooth pasting. Outward-normal-first tuple at the south pole has sign (-1)^(m+1); reflected charts realize either sign. Empty family gives degree zero. Exact regular-value degree supplier requires the now-stated nonempty connected oriented source. Only finite choice is used.

entry.title: The mod-two degree of a map to a sphere
entry.statement:
Let $M$ be a closed smooth $m$-manifold with $m\ge1$, so that $M$ is compact
and has empty boundary ([[def-smooth-manifold]], [[def-compact-space]]), and let
$f:M\to S^m$ be smooth, where $S^m\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+1}$ is the Euclidean
unit sphere ([[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]]). A point $y\in S^m$ is
a **regular value** of $f$ when every point of $f^{-1}(y)$ is a regular point
of $f$ ([[def-regular-and-critical-points-and-values]]). For a regular value
$y$ of $f$ define
$$\deg_2(f):=|f^{-1}(y)|\bmod 2\;\in\;\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z,$$
the **mod-two degree** of $f$, the parity of the number of points of the
regular fibre, computed in the quotient set $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$
([[def-integers-modulo-n]]). The empty fibre is allowed and contributes the
parity of the empty set, namely $0$; in particular a constant map has mod-two
degree $0$, since a value different from its image has empty fibre and is
vacuously regular.

No orientation of $M$ is required, and no orientation of $S^m$ is used: only
the *number* of points of the fibre enters. This is what distinguishes the
invariant from the integer degree of
[[def-degree-of-a-proper-smooth-map-by-compact-support-cohomology]], which is
defined for oriented source and target and counts points with signs. When $M$
is nonempty, connected and oriented and $m\ge1$, the signed count of the same fibre is the integer
degree of $f$ by [[thm-regular-value-formula-for-degree]], and reducing that
identity modulo two gives $\deg_2(f)\equiv\deg(f)\pmod2$.

Two things are *not* asserted by this definition and are proved in
[[lem-mod-two-degree-is-well-defined-and-homotopy-invariant]], which is why
that lemma is recorded in `justified_by`. First, the parity of the fibre is
independent of the regular value chosen, so the notation $\deg_2(f)$ denotes a
single element of $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ rather than a value attached to a
pair $(f,y)$; until that is known, the displayed formula defines a candidate
value for each supplied regular value. Second, homotopic maps have equal
mod-two degree, so $\deg_2$ descends to free homotopy classes.

The fibre is finite whenever $y$ is a regular value, so the parity is a
cardinality of a finite set and no cardinal arithmetic is involved. Indeed,
every $p\in f^{-1}(y)$ is a regular point, and since $\dim M=\dim S^m=m$ the
differential $df_p$ is an isomorphism of tangent spaces; the inverse function
theorem for smooth maps of manifolds
([[thm-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-on-manifolds]]) then makes $f$ a local
diffeomorphism at $p$, so $f$ is injective on some neighbourhood of $p$ and the
fibre is discrete in the sense that each of its points is isolated in it. The
fibre is closed because $f$ is continuous ([[prop-smooth-maps-are-continuous]])
and $\{y\}$ is closed, and a closed discrete subset of the compact space $M$ is
finite: the family consisting of $M\smallsetminus f^{-1}(y)$ and of all open neighbourhoods meeting the fibre in exactly one point is an open cover of the compact space $M$, and a finite subcover selects finitely many of those neighbourhoods, each meeting the fibre in exactly one point, so the fibre is finite.
Assuming $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), regular values exist by Sard's theorem for smooth manifolds
([[thm-morse-sard-for-smooth-manifolds]]), whose statement in this library
assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; this definition
itself makes no choice and uses no orientation, and the choice assumption
enters only through the existence of regular values and through the
well-definedness lemma.
entry.strategy: Checked candidate parity for supplied regular values on every closed m-manifold, m>=1, including empty and disconnected M. Inverse-function isolation plus all isolating neighbourhoods and compactness proves finiteness without indexed choice. Constant-map empty fibre gives zero. Comparison with scalar degree is restricted to nonempty connected oriented M, as the exact regular-value formula requires. Sard and well-definedness carry AC_omega; justified_by defers invariance. Reader's domain and choice corrections are retained.

entry.title: The mod-two degree is well defined and homotopy invariant
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed smooth $m$-manifold,
$m\ge1$, and let $f,g:M\to S^m$ be smooth. (i) Any two regular values $y,y'$ of
$f$ give the same parity $|f^{-1}(y)|\equiv|f^{-1}(y')|\pmod2$, so $\deg_2(f)$
is well defined. (ii) If $f$ and $g$ are homotopic, equivalently smoothly
homotopic, then $\deg_2(f)=\deg_2(g)$; hence $\deg_2$ is defined on free
homotopy classes of continuous maps $[M,S^m]$. (iii) If $M$ is nonempty, connected and oriented then
$\deg_2(f)\equiv\deg(f)\pmod2$.
entry.strategy: The authored proof uses universal compact-one-manifold boundary parity, not the nonorientable-only classification. Regular-value/basis independence yields parity equality for arbitrary closed M, including empty/disconnected sources. Sard, finite null union and positive-dimensional dense complement supply a common regular value for both endpoints; no endpoint regularity follows from homotopy regularity. Smoothing continuous representatives and homotopies proves independent extension to free classes. Reduction of signed count is limited to nonempty connected oriented M. Exact suppliers preserve AC_omega and m>=1.

entry.title: The Hopf degree classification for oriented domains
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a nonempty closed connected oriented smooth
$m$-manifold, $m\ge1$. (i) Two smooth maps $f,g:M\to S^m$ are smoothly
homotopic if and only if $\deg(f)=\deg(g)$; equivalently degree induces a
bijection from smooth homotopy classes to $\mathbb Z$. (ii) Every integer
occurs as $\deg(f)$ for some smooth $f:M\to S^m$. (iii) Consequently degree
induces a bijection from the set $[M,S^m]$ of free homotopy classes of
continuous maps to $\mathbb Z$: two continuous maps $M\to S^m$ are homotopic
if and only if they have the same degree. Here the degree of a continuous map is the degree of any homotopic smooth representative; part (i) and the approximation theorems make this independent of the representative.
entry.strategy: Checked both directions independently: compact source makes the combined smooth homotopy proper, so the exact degree-invariance theorem applies. Equal degrees give equal signed counts at independently supplied regular values, then the proved zero-framed classification and collapse comparison give a smooth homotopy. Surjectivity is the explicit finite-ball realization. Continuous degree is defined by a homotopic smooth representative, and smooth-endpoint homotopy smoothing proves independence. Nonempty closed connected oriented M, m>=1 and AC_omega match every supplier; zero degree/constant maps included. Freed Theorem 2.37 and Milnor Section 7 agree, but the authored proof supplies the assembly.

entry.title: The mod-two degree classification for nonorientable domains
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed connected nonorientable smooth
$m$-manifold, $m\ge1$. (i) Two smooth maps $f,g:M\to S^m$ are smoothly
homotopic if and only if $\deg_2(f)=\deg_2(g)$. (ii) Both elements of
$\mathbb Z/2$ are realized: constant maps have mod-two degree $0$, and the
pinch map of a closed coordinate ball has mod-two degree $1$. (iii)
Consequently $\deg_2$ induces a bijection $[M,S^m]\to\mathbb Z/2$, so two
continuous maps $M\to S^m$ are homotopic if and only if their mod-two degrees
agree.
entry.strategy: Parity homotopy invariance proves the forward direction; equal parity yields framed-cobordant regular fibres by the independently reviewed nonorientable classification, hence smooth homotopy by collapse comparison. The one-ball construction uses only the local smooth model and gluing phases of the realization proof, which do not need global orientability; its single regular fibre has parity one. Constant maps give zero. Continuous representatives and homotopy smoothing justify both independence and the free-class bijection. Nonorientability implies nonempty M and m>=2, so endpoint cases match prerequisites. AC_omega explicitly carried.

entry.title: Connectedness is needed for a single degree invariant
entry.statement:
Connectedness is load-bearing in both Hopf classifications of this page,
[[thm-hopf-degree-classification-for-oriented-domains]] and
[[thm-hopf-mod-two-degree-classification-for-nonorientable-domains]]
([[def-connected-space]]). If a closed oriented smooth $m$-manifold $M$ is not
connected, each connected component is itself a closed connected oriented
$m$-manifold, a smooth map $M\to S^m$ has one signed degree contribution on
each component, and the total degree is the sum of these contributions; but a
homotopy of maps of $M$ restricts to a homotopy on each component, so the
componentwise degrees are invariants that a single integer need not capture. For a disconnected source with nonorientable components, the same invariance remark applies to their mod-two degrees. Orientable components retain their integer degrees; calling the whole source nonorientable does not make every component nonorientable.
The classification theorems of this page therefore assume connectedness, and
the counterexample on the companion page exhibits two maps of a disconnected
closed oriented domain whose total degrees agree while the maps are not
homotopic. No claim is made here that every disconnected domain admits a
finer classification by the vector of componentwise degrees and their homotopy
types; the recorded fact is only the failure of the total degree as a single
complete invariant, witnessed by the companion counterexample
([[def-degree-of-a-proper-smooth-map-by-compact-support-cohomology]],
[[def-homotopy-relative-and-path-homotopy]]).
entry.strategy: Each component of a closed smooth source is open and closed and compact, with finitely many components by compactness. A fixed-source homotopy restricts to each component, preserving its integer degree when oriented and parity when nonorientable. Total degree here means the sum of scalar component degrees; it is not an application of the connected-source scalar definition. The corrected mixed-orientability caveat is essential: one nonorientable component does not replace every oriented component's integer invariant by parity. The companion counterexample supplies failure of a single total invariant.

entry.title: Closedness is needed for the Hopf degree classification
entry.statement:
The Hopf classification of [[thm-hopf-degree-classification-for-oriented-domains]] assumes a nonempty compact source without boundary. For a compact manifold with boundary, prescribing values on that boundary is additional data, and a relative classification requires a separate statement for maps and homotopies of pairs ([[def-smooth-chart-atlas-and-structure-on-a-manifold-with-boundary]]). No such relative classification is proved on this page.

For a noncompact source $M$ there is no proper map $M\to S^m$: the inverse image of the compact target is all of $M$, which properness would require to be compact. Thus the proper-map degree of [[def-degree-of-a-proper-smooth-map-by-compact-support-cohomology]] cannot be applied to such a sphere map. For maps to other, noncompact targets the cited definition requires properness, and [[thm-degree-is-invariant-under-proper-smooth-homotopy]] requires properness of the combined homotopy. These are separate settings; this page asserts no classification there ([[def-compact-space]]).
entry.strategy: The corrected remark accurately states the nonempty compact boundaryless scope. No proper map from a noncompact M to compact S^m exists, since its whole source is the inverse image of the compact target. Combined-homotopy properness and boundary-relative data are separate necessary settings in the exact cited degree definition/invariance theorem. No unsupported relative classification is asserted.

entry.title: Circle power maps are classified by their exponent
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). For $k\in\mathbb Z$ let $p_k:S^1\to S^1$, $p_k(z)=z^k$ (equivalently
$p_k([t])=[kt]$), with the counterclockwise orientations. Then
$\deg(p_k)=k$, and by the Hopf classification for $M=S^1$ the maps $p_k$ and
$p_l$ are homotopic if and only if $k=l$. Hence the homotopy classes
$[S^1,S^1]$ are in bijection with $\mathbb Z$ and the class of a power map is
determined by its exponent, consistently with the covering-space computation
of circle self-maps.
entry.strategy: Read complete published power-map computation: positive k gives k preimages of + sign, negative k gives |k| of - sign, and zero uses empty regular fibre at [1/2]. The displayed lift t to kt is a lift of p_k composed with the universal covering R to S^1, not a lift of p_k itself. Period increment equals k; sphere free-homotopy classification for m=1 gives necessity and sufficiency and exhausts every degree. Counterclockwise and quotient-circle orientations agree; AC_omega inherited for classification.

entry.title: A sphere reflection has degree minus one
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). For $m\ge1$ let $R(x_0,x_1,\dots,x_m)=(-x_0,x_1,\dots,x_m)$ be the coordinate
reflection of $S^m$, oriented by the outward-normal-first boundary orientation
of $S^m=\partial D^{m+1}$. Then $R$ is a smooth diffeomorphism of $S^m$
reversing orientation, so $\deg(R)=-1$; by the sphere classification every
self-map of $S^m$ of degree $-1$ is homotopic to $R$, and by the
homotopy-equivalence corollary a self-map of $S^m$ of degree $-1$ is a
homotopy equivalence exactly when it is homotopic to a reflection.
entry.strategy: Ambient coordinate reflection preserves the sphere and sends its outward normal to the outward normal while reversing ambient determinant, so it reverses tangent boundary orientation and is a smooth involution. Exact diffeomorphism-degree theorem gives -1 for all m>=1. Hopf sphere classification identifies every degree -1 map with its class in both directions, and the +/-1 corollary gives homotopy equivalence. m=0 excluded; AC_omega inherited. No antipodal sign is substituted for a single-coordinate reflection.

entry.title: Collapsing $k$ oriented disks realizes degree $k$
entry.statement:
Let $M$ be a nonempty closed connected oriented smooth $m$-manifold, $m\ge1$, and let
$k\in\mathbb Z$. Pick $|k|$ pairwise disjoint closed coordinate balls in $M$.
On each ball read the explicit smooth pinch model $F$ of [[lem-every-integer-degree-is-realized-by-a-map-to-the-sphere]] through a chart centred at that ball. Choose the chart sign so that $\operatorname{sgn}(dF_0)\operatorname{sgn}(d\varphi_i)=\operatorname{sgn}(k)$; for this outward-normal-first sphere orientation, $\operatorname{sgn}(dF_0)=(-1)^{m+1}$. Extend by the same base point $N$ outside the balls. The resulting smooth map $f_k:M\to S^m$ has the point $y_-=F(0)$ of
the model as a regular value whose preimage is exactly the set of centres of
the chosen balls, one point per ball, so that
$\deg(f_k)=\sum_{i=1}^{|k|}\operatorname{sgn}(df_{k,p_i})$. Choosing all local
signs to be $\operatorname{sgn}(k)$ gives $\deg(f_k)=k$. For $k=\pm1$ this is
the pinch of a single oriented ball, and for $k=0$ the empty family gives the
constant map, of degree $0$.
entry.strategy: The exact earlier realization construction supplies open disjoint chart supports and smooth model F. Verified regular fibre consists of |k| centres, chart sign compensates model sign (-1)^(m+1), and the regular-value formula gives k. Empty balls give constant degree zero; positive and negative one-ball cases work. Nonempty closed connected oriented and m>=1 hypotheses match the supplier.

entry.title: Maps from even projective space to the sphere use mod-two degree
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$ be even. Then $\mathbb{RP}^n$ is a closed connected nonorientable
smooth $n$-manifold, and the collapse map
$q:\mathbb{RP}^n\to\mathbb{RP}^n/\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}\cong S^n$ has mod-two
degree $1$. The smooth representative $\widetilde q$ constructed below has $y_-=(0,\ldots,0,-1)$ as a regular value with the single preimage $\pi(0)$. The quotient map $q$ itself is continuous; it is not asserted to be globally smooth.
Constant maps have mod-two degree $0$. Consequently $[\mathbb{RP}^n,S^n]\cong
\mathbb Z/2$, with the two classes represented by $q$ and by a constant map,
and the mod-two degree is a complete invariant of free homotopy classes; no
integer degree is available because $\mathbb{RP}^n$ is nonorientable.
entry.strategy: Read actual projective cellular attachment and orientability proofs. The top hemisphere model attaches along the antipodal equator and its interior parametrization followed by the covering is locally diffeomorphic. The classical pinch c is a continuous quotient homeomorphism, with the displayed inverse valid at the south pole. Smooth F is constant on a collar, hence descends to a globally smooth representative. Interpolated W_tau equals s near zero, stays in [0,1], and fixes the boundary; compact-source/Hausdorff-target quotient of pi times I gives a continuous descended homotopy. Its single regular preimage has parity one; constants have zero. For even n>=2, closed connected nonorientable hypotheses permit Hopf classification. Full AC in the supplier is only its final field-duality claim, unused here; attachment steps are choice-free. AC_omega carried for smoothing/classification.

entry.title: Equal total degree does not classify maps from a disconnected domain
entry.statement:
For every closed oriented smooth $m$-manifold $M$, possibly disconnected, two
maps $M\to S^m$ are homotopic if and only if their total degree, the sum of the
signed degrees on the connected components, agrees. Counterexample: for $m\ge1$
take $M=S^m\sqcup S^m$, let $c$ be a constant map of $S^m$ into $S^m$, and put
$f=\operatorname{id}\sqcup\,c$ and $g=c\sqcup\operatorname{id}$. Both maps have
total degree $1$, but they are not homotopic.
entry.strategy: On two separately oriented copies of S^m, m>=1, id/constant restrictions have degrees (1,0) and (0,1); total is explicitly their sum. Restricting any proposed continuous homotopy to the first component contradicts homological sphere-degree invariance. Exact regular-value supplier identifies these smooth degrees with homological degree, so this obstruction does not require homotopy smoothing or AC_omega. Empty-fibre degree zero and identity degree one are supplied choice-free; connected-source scalar definition is not applied to the disjoint union. Counterexample retains both components.

entry.title: A closed discrete subset of a compact space is finite
entry.statement: Let $X$ be a compact topological space ([[def-compact-space]]) and let $S\subseteq X$ be closed and discrete, meaning that for every $s\in S$ there is an open $U_s\subseteq X$ with $U_s\cap S=\{s\}$ ([[def-subspace-topology-top]], [[def-topological-space]]). Then $S$ is finite.
entry.strategy: Since $S$ is closed, $X\setminus S$ is open. The family $\{X\setminus S\}\cup\{U_s:s\in S\}$ is an open cover of $X$: a point of $S$ lies in its own $U_s$ and a point of $X\setminus S$ lies in $X\setminus S$. Compactness extracts a finite subcover; if $U_{s_1},\dots,U_{s_k}$ are the subcover members coming from $S$, then every point of $S$ lies in some $U_{s_j}$ (it cannot lie in $X\setminus S$), hence $S\subseteq\{s_1,\dots,s_k\}$ and $S$ is finite. No choice principle and no uniformity of the neighbourhoods is used; the argument is the compactness step in the finiteness of fixed point sets.

entry.title: Fixed points are exactly the intersections of the graph with the diagonal
entry.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and $f:M\to M$ a smooth map ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) with graph $\Gamma_f=\{(x,f(x)):x\in M\}\subseteq M\times M$ ([[prop-the-graph-of-a-smooth-map-is-an-embedded-submanifold]]) and diagonal $\Delta_M=\{(x,x):x\in M\}$ ([[def-the-diagonal-of-a-space]], [[prop-the-diagonal-is-an-embedded-submanifold]]). Then for every $x\in M$,
$$x\in\operatorname{Fix}(f)\iff(x,f(x))\in\Gamma_f\cap\Delta_M\iff(x,x)\in\Gamma_f,$$
so the graph map $\gamma_f:M\to M\times M$, $\gamma_f(x)=(x,f(x))$, satisfies $\gamma_f^{-1}(\Delta_M)=\{(x,x):x\in\operatorname{Fix}(f)\}$: fixed points of $f$ are exactly the intersections of the graph with the diagonal.
entry.strategy: Immediate from the definitions: $(x,f(x))\in\Delta_M$ means $x=f(x)$, and the three displayed conditions are the same equation. No smoothness beyond the existence of the objects, and no choice principle, is used; the empty and zero-dimensional cases are included.

references.locator: Ch. 3 §4, printed p. 119 (a fixed point is precisely an intersection point of graph(f) with the diagonal)

entry.title: Nondegenerate fixed point
entry.statement: Let $M$ be a smooth $n$-manifold and let $f:M\to M$ be a smooth map with a fixed point $x$; identify $T_{f(x)}M$ with $T_xM$ along $f(x)=x$, so that the differential is an endomorphism $Df_x:T_xM\to T_xM$ ([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]). The fixed point $x$ is **nondegenerate** when $I-Df_x$ is an isomorphism of $T_xM$ ([[def-linear-isomorphism-and-invertible-linear-map]]), equivalently when $1$ is not an eigenvalue of $Df_x$. A nondegenerate fixed point is isolated: in a chart at $x$ the displacement $u\mapsto u-\widehat f(u)$ has invertible derivative $I-D\widehat f(0)$ at $u=0$, hence is a local diffeomorphism near $0$ ([[thm-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-on-manifolds]]) with the unique zero $0$ there, so a neighbourhood of $x$ contains no other fixed point. No choice principle is used, and $n=0$ is allowed (then $I-Df_x$ is an isomorphism of the zero space and the condition is vacuous).
entry.strategy: Definition of the linearization condition, with isolatedness supplied by the inverse function theorem, in the exact form used by the local index of [[def-local-fixed-point-index]]. The convention is $I-Df_x$, not $Df_x-I$; with the other ordering the determinant changes by the sign $(-1)^n$. No orientation of $M$ is used.

references.locator: Ch. 3 §4, printed pp. 120-121 (the Lefschetz condition: df_x-I an isomorphism; Lefschetz points are isolated)

entry.title: Graph-diagonal transversality is exactly fixed-point nondegeneracy
entry.strategy: In the splitting $T_{(x,x)}(M\times M)=T_xM\oplus T_xM$ the tangent space of $\Gamma_f$ at $\gamma_f(x)$ is the graph $\{(v,Df_xv):v\in T_xM\}$ and that of $\Delta_M$ is the diagonal $\{(v,v)\}$; both are $n$-dimensional, so transversality is equivalent to the two subspaces meeting only in $0$. A vector forms $(v,v)=(w,Df_xw)$ exactly when $v=w$ and $(I-Df_x)v=0$; the intersection is therefore $\{(v,v):(I-Df_x)v=0\}$, which is zero precisely when $I-Df_x$ is injective, hence invertible in finite dimension ([[def-linear-isomorphism-and-invertible-linear-map]]). Points over non-fixed points are not in the diagonal, so transversality there is vacuous and the global equivalence follows. No orientation, metric or choice principle is used.

entry.title: Isolated fixed point and local fixed point index
entry.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth $n$-manifold without boundary, $n\ge1$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let $f:M\to M$ be a smooth map ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) and let $x$ be an **isolated** fixed point of $f$, i.e. some neighbourhood of $x$ contains no other fixed point. Choose a chart $(\varphi,U)$ with $x\in U$ and $\varphi(x)=0$ ([[def-manifold-chart-coordinate-domain-and-coordinate-functions]]) and $\varepsilon>0$ with $B_\varepsilon(0)\subseteq\varphi(U)$ and $\widehat f(u):=\varphi(f(\varphi^{-1}(u)))\neq u$ for $0<|u|<\varepsilon$, and set $g(u):=u-\widehat f(u)$. The **local fixed point index** of $f$ at $x$ is the degree
$$\operatorname{ind}_x(f):=\deg\Bigl(S^{n-1}\to S^{n-1},\ v\mapsto\frac{g(\varepsilon v)}{|g(\varepsilon v)|}\Bigr)\in\mathbb Z$$
of [[def-degree-of-a-map-between-oriented-closed-manifolds]], both spheres carrying their standard orientations. The value is independent of the radius by [[thm-degree-is-invariant-under-proper-smooth-homotopy]] and of the chart, the ball and the neighbourhood by [[lem-local-fixed-point-index-is-coordinate-and-neighbourhood-independent]]; it uses no orientation of $M$, because a chart change multiplies source and target orientations by the same sign. The empty sum over a fixed-point-free map is $0$ by convention, and every statement on this page assumes $n\ge1$.
entry.strategy: Definition by the Euclidean displacement model and the sphere degree, in the exact form of [[def-isolated-zero-and-local-index-of-a-vector-field]] applied to the chart displacement field; well-definedness is deferred to [[lem-local-fixed-point-index-is-coordinate-and-neighbourhood-independent]] in the style of DT-11's intersection sign. No choice principle is used.

entry.title: The local fixed point index is invariant under conjugation by a local diffeomorphism
entry.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth $n$-manifold without boundary, $n\ge1$, let $f:M\to M$ have an isolated fixed point $x$, let $h:N\to M$ be a diffeomorphism from a neighbourhood of $y\in N$ onto a neighbourhood of $x$ with $h(y)=x$, and let $f':=h^{-1}\circ f\circ h$ (defined near $y$) have the isolated fixed point $y$. Then
$$\operatorname{ind}_y(f')=\operatorname{ind}_x(f)$$
([[def-local-fixed-point-index]]). In particular, if $\pi:\widetilde M\to M$ is a covering map, $\widetilde f$ is a lift of $f$ ($\pi\circ\widetilde f=f\circ\pi$) and $\widetilde x$ is a fixed point of $\widetilde f$ with $\pi(\widetilde x)=x$, then $\operatorname{ind}_{\widetilde x}(\widetilde f)=\operatorname{ind}_x(f)$ whenever $x$ is an isolated fixed point of $f$.
entry.strategy: Choose charts near $x$ and $y$ in which $h$ becomes the identity of a Euclidean ball: in these charts the displacement representatives $u-\widehat f(u)$ of $f$ and $f'$ coincide, so the normalized sphere maps are literally the same and their degrees agree. For the covering case, $\pi$ restricts to a diffeomorphism from a neighbourhood of $\widetilde x$ onto a neighbourhood of $x$ and conjugates $\widetilde f$ to $f$ there, so the first clause applies. The statement transports local indices across the orientation double cover in [[lem-fixed-point-sum-of-the-two-lifts-of-a-self-map]]; no orientation of either manifold and no choice principle are used.

references.title: Victor Guillemin and Alan Pollack, Differential Topology (Prentice-Hall 1974; complete 236-page PDF)
references.locator: Ch. 3 §5, printed p. 136 (the local number is invariant under diffeomorphic reparametrization)

entry.title: The local fixed point index is independent of chart, ball and neighbourhood
entry.statement: Let $M$ be a smooth $n$-manifold without boundary, $n\ge1$, and let $f:M\to M$ be smooth with an isolated fixed point $x$. Then the choices entering [[def-local-fixed-point-index]] do not affect the value: any two admissible charts at $x$, and any two admissible radii in one chart, produce homotopic normalized sphere maps and hence the same degree. Consequently $\operatorname{ind}_x(f)$ is a well-defined integer depending only on the germ of $f$ at $x$, and it is computed by the displayed formula in every chart and every sufficiently small ball around $x$.
entry.strategy: Radius: for $0<\varepsilon'<\varepsilon$ the normalizations $v\mapsto g(\varepsilon v)/|g(\varepsilon v)|$ and $v\mapsto g(\varepsilon'v)/|g(\varepsilon'v)|$ are homotopic through $v\mapsto g(t\varepsilon v)/|g(t\varepsilon v)|$, which is nonzero throughout because $g\neq0$ on $0<|u|<\varepsilon$; degree invariance is [[thm-degree-is-invariant-under-proper-smooth-homotopy]]. Charts: let $A=d(\psi\circ\varphi^{-1})_0$, an isomorphism of $\mathbb R^n$ ([[cor-the-differential-of-a-diffeomorphism-is-an-isomorphism]]). The two displacement representatives are related by the transition near $0$, so their normalized maps differ by a reparametrization $v\mapsto Av/|Av|$ of the source sphere and by the corresponding normalization of the target; both have degree $\operatorname{sign}\det A$ ([[thm-regular-value-formula-for-degree]], [[prop-degree-of-an-orientation-preserving-or-reversing-diffeomorphism]]), and by multiplicativity of degree ([[prop-degree-is-multiplicative-under-composition]]) the two factors cancel, so the degrees agree. Neighbourhoods are compared through a common smaller ball. The argument is the chart-independence proof of [[lem-vector-field-index-is-independent-of-chart-ball-and-trivialization]] in the fixed point language, and it uses no orientation of $M$.

entry.title: The index of a nondegenerate fixed point is the sign of det(I-Df)
entry.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth $n$-manifold without boundary, $n\ge1$, and let $x$ be a nondegenerate fixed point of a smooth map $f:M\to M$ ([[def-nondegenerate-fixed-point]]). Then
$$\operatorname{ind}_x(f)=\operatorname{sign}\det(I-Df_x:T_xM\to T_xM)\in\{+1,-1\},$$
so every nondegenerate fixed point has index $+1$ or $-1$. The convention is $I-Df_x$, not $Df_x-I$; in the other ordering the value is multiplied by $(-1)^n$, which is the source of sign discrepancies between references.
entry.strategy: Work in a chart at $x$ and put $\widehat f=\varphi\circ f\circ\varphi^{-1}$, $g(u)=u-\widehat f(u)$. Then $g$ is a smooth vector field on the chart ball (a smooth section of the trivial tangent bundle, [[def-induced-tangent-bundle-chart]]) with $g(0)=0$ and vertical derivative $Dg_0=I-Df_x$ invertible ([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]], [[def-nondegenerate-zero-of-a-vector-field]]). By [[def-isolated-zero-and-local-index-of-a-vector-field]] the vector field index $\operatorname{ind}_0g$ is exactly the degree of $v\mapsto g(\varepsilon v)/|g(\varepsilon v)|$, which is $\operatorname{ind}_x(f)$ by [[def-local-fixed-point-index]]; hence $\operatorname{ind}_x(f)=\operatorname{ind}_0g$ by [[lem-local-fixed-point-index-is-coordinate-and-neighbourhood-independent]]. The in-run theorem [[thm-index-of-a-nondegenerate-vector-field-zero]] gives $\operatorname{ind}_0g=\operatorname{sign}\det Dg_0=\operatorname{sign}\det(I-Df_x)$. No orientation of $M$ and no choice principle are used.

references.title: Peter Wong, Lectures on Fixed Point Theory, Mini-Course XV Encontro Brasileiro de Topologia, Rio Claro 2006 (complete notes)
